patients.summary: Retired library administrator with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone, osteoporosis and hypertension. Over seven years with the practice she develops anemia of chronic disease, a right Baker's cyst, chronic-phase CML treated with imatinib, and in 2026 diffuse alveolar hemorrhage that ends methotrexate. Outside records reach the chart thinly.

Take 1 tablet (600 mg elemental calcium) by mouth twice daily

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
57F moving her primary care here; her old office is a long drive from Chesterfield and her husband's plan covers us. Pleasant, organized, brought a typed med list.

PMH:
- Rheumatoid arthritis, managed by her outside rheumatologist. Joints have been quiet on weekly methotrexate plus prednisone 5 mg. Sees rheum every few months.
- Osteoporosis by DXA at the old office (report requested). Takes calcium and D3.
- Hypertension on lisinopril 10 mg, home readings 120s-130s/70s-80s per her log.
PSH: bilateral carpal tunnel releases earlier this year, healed, numbness gone.
Meds: methotrexate 20 mg once weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily, prednisone 5 mg daily, ibuprofen 400 mg q6h prn joint pain (uses it a couple of times a week), calcium carbonate 600 mg BID, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfa drugs - rash. Latex - contact dermatitis (gloves).
FH: mother with RA. Father type 2 DM. Paternal uncle had CLL.
SH: retired library administrator. Married. Smoked about 8 pack-years, stopped in 2010. No alcohol at all since starting methotrexate. Walks most mornings.

ROS: no fevers, weight change, chest pain, dyspnea, GI bleeding. Mild morning stiffness under 20 minutes.

Exam: well-appearing. BP as recorded. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Hands with well-healed carpal tunnel scars, no synovitis at MCPs/PIPs/wrists today. Knees without effusion. No edema.

A/P:
1. RA - stable on MTX/pred per rheum. Will do the quarterly CBC/CMP here if rheum is fine with that (she'd prefer not to drive to their lab). Baseline today.
2. HTN - at goal, continue lisinopril.
3. Osteoporosis on chronic steroid - calcium/D. Getting the old DXA.
4. Health maintenance: hep C and HIV screen today, lipids. Requesting colonoscopy, Pap and mammogram records. Flu shot in October.
Follow up in about 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Diane - everything from Tuesday looks fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver numbers are all where they should be on methotrexate, cholesterol is good, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Rheumatology clinic - visit of 10/20/2020

Dear colleague,

I saw our mutual patient for routine RA follow-up. Her joints are behaving: no flares, pain controlled on methotrexate 20 mg weekly. The new issue is about two months of tiredness and feeling weak.

She looked pale. No splenomegaly or hepatomegaly by palpation and no nodes in the cervical, axillary or inguinal chains. No synovitis.

Labs today: Hgb 10.2, MCV 84. Iron 30, TIBC 200, saturation 15%, ferritin 150.

The low iron with a low TIBC and a ferritin in the normal range reads to me as anemia of chronic disease rather than iron deficiency. I have not started iron. Continuing methotrexate, folic acid and prednisone 5 mg as before. We will keep an eye on the counts with her quarterly labs at your office.

Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex.

With thanks,
Rheumatology

O: Vitals as charted. A bit pale at the conjunctivae. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no spleen or liver edge. No nodes. No active synovitis.
Rheum labs 10/20: Hgb 10.2, MCV 84, Fe 30, TIBC 200, sat 15%, ferritin 150. Our September CBC was a little low too, which I had not flagged.
A/P: Anemia of chronic disease in the setting of RA, agree with rheum. Colonoscopy 2017 clean. Repeat CBC today, then continue the quarterly MTX labs and watch the trend. Return sooner if lightheaded, short of breath, or any bleeding.

Noticed a lump behind the R knee about a week ago when sitting cross-legged. Not painful. Maybe an ache at the end of a long walk. No fall or twist. No calf pain, no leg swelling.
Exam: soft fullness in the R popliteal fossa, nontender. No erythema or warmth. Calf soft, nontender, no asymmetry. Knee without effusion, ROM full.
Impression: likely popliteal cyst given RA; want it looked at properly and a clot excluded. Referred to orthopedics - she prefers the group that did her left knee; they can image there. Call right away if calf pain or sudden swelling.
Flu vaccine today.

conditions.label: Synovial cyst of popliteal space [Baker], right knee

reports.text: Right lower extremity. Common femoral, femoral, popliteal and posterior tibial veins compressible with normal phasic flow and augmentation. No intraluminal thrombus. In the popliteal fossa there is a well-defined cystic structure with a neck that communicates with the knee joint.
reports.conclusion: No right lower extremity DVT. Popliteal (Baker's) cyst communicating with the knee joint.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, bruises.
HPI: 60F with RA on MTX/pred. Over roughly two months the tiredness she's had for years has gotten clearly worse - naps most afternoons now. Bruises on her shins and forearms without any bump she can remember. No nosebleeds, no gum bleeding, no blood in stool or urine. No fevers or drenching sweats. Missed her March lab draw.
Meds: unchanged. Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Exam: pale. Several 2-4 cm ecchymoses of varying age on both shins and the L forearm. No petechiae. No cervical, axillary or inguinal nodes. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen: spleen tip palpable below the L costal margin on inspiration, nontender; liver edge not felt. No synovitis.
A/P: Fatigue, bruising, palpable spleen. CBC and CMP stat today.

Addendum 14:45: CBC back - WBC 86.4, Hgb 9.4, plt 512. Lab smear review: left-shifted myeloid cells. Called pt. Urgent heme/onc referral placed and I called their office directly - seen within the month.

documents.title: Result Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with Diane and her husband on speaker. Explained the white count is very high with immature cells and she needs a blood specialist promptly; it may be a bone-marrow disorder and they will likely need a marrow sample. She asked if it is leukemia - told her that is one of the possibilities and the specialist will sort it out quickly. Bleeding/fever precautions. Heme office will call her tomorrow.

documents.body: Heme/onc confirmed new-patient visit 4/17. Records and labs faxed.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Consultation
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Hematology & Oncology - new patient seen 04/17/2023

Thank you for sending Ms. Berman, 60, with RA (methotrexate, prednisone 5 mg), osteoporosis and hypertension, previously evaluated for anemia of chronic disease and a right popliteal cyst. Over three months she has had steadily worsening fatigue, an enlarged spleen and bruising without explanation.

Peripheral smear here shows a striking excess of myeloid cells across all stages of maturation, mature and immature. A bone marrow aspirate and biopsy were done in clinic; the aspirate is hypercellular with a myeloid predominance.

This picture raises concern for a clonal myeloid neoplasm. Cytogenetics, BCR-ABL1 FISH and quantitative BCR-ABL1 PCR have been sent from the marrow. We will see her as soon as they return.

Medications reviewed: methotrexate 20 mg weekly, folic acid, prednisone 5 mg, ibuprofen as needed, calcium, vitamin D3, lisinopril 10 mg. Allergies: sulfonamides (rash), latex.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.title: Outside Letter Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Heme consult reviewed. Marrow studies pending.

documents.title: Results from hematology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The hematologist called today. It's chronic myeloid leukemia, the type with the Philadelphia chromosome. She says it is early (chronic phase) and that there is a daily pill that works well for most people. I start it Monday. I'm a bit shaken but she was very reassuring. Wanted you to know. Do I need to stop anything you prescribe?

documents.title: RE: Results from hematology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Diane, I'm so sorry you got this news, and I'm glad it was caught in chronic phase - the pills for CML really do work well. Your lisinopril is fine to continue. Rheumatology and hematology will coordinate on the methotrexate. Let's do a video visit in a couple of weeks once you've started so we can go over everything.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with food and a full glass of water

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Hematology & Oncology - update

Marrow results (reported 04/26/2023): BCR-ABL1 fusion detected by FISH in 88% of nuclei. Quantitative RT-PCR: BCR-ABL1 (p210) 64% on the International Scale. Findings consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia, chronic phase.

She started imatinib 400 mg once daily on 05/01/2023. We will check counts every two weeks initially and BCR-ABL1 PCR at 3, 6 and 12 months. Methotrexate, folic acid and prednisone may continue per rheumatology; we will follow her counts closely.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Hematology & Oncology - visit 04/15/2025

CML, chronic phase, on imatinib 400 mg daily since May 2023.

Two months of fatigue and breathlessness with exertion. Remains on methotrexate and low-dose prednisone for RA. On exam she is pale; no active joint inflammation.

Hgb 10.2, MCV 82. Iron 30, TIBC 250 (saturation 12%), ferritin 200. Reticulocytes 1%.
BCR-ABL1 0.02% IS - deep molecular response maintained.

Impression: the anemia fits chronic inflammation rather than iron deficiency, with an underproductive marrow response. Leukemia well controlled. Continue imatinib 400 mg. No iron and no transfusion indicated. Recheck in 6 months.

Medications per our list: imatinib, methotrexate, folic acid, ibuprofen as needed, calcium carbonate, vitamin D3, lisinopril.
Allergies: sulfonamides, latex.

Hematology & Oncology

documents.body:
ED visit 04/15/2026 (faxed summary)

63-year-old woman with RA on methotrexate and prednisone and CML on imatinib, two weeks of worsening breathlessness, dry cough and low-grade temperatures. No travel. No sick contacts.

RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. Tachypneic. Crackles at both bases.

WBC 9.0, Hgb 13.2, plt 250. CRP 25 mg/L, ESR 40, LDH 220.
CXR: bilateral interstitial infiltrates. HRCT chest: diffuse ground-glass opacities; no PE; no lymphadenopathy.

PMH per our system: RA, CML, chronic anemia, Baker's cyst, osteoporosis, HTN.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.

Disposition: admitted to medicine with pulmonology consultation.

medications.reason: stopped during admission for diffuse alveolar hemorrhage

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) daily for 14 days, then decrease by 10 mg every 14 days to 10 mg; then resume usual prednisone 5 mg daily

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 04/15/2026 - discharged 04/21/2026

Diagnosis: diffuse alveolar hemorrhage; cause not established.

Course: Admitted from the ED with hypoxemia and diffuse ground-glass change. Pulmonology performed bronchoscopy on 04/16: sequential BAL aliquots returned progressively bloodier, and hemosiderin-laden macrophages were seen. BAL bacterial, fungal and AFB cultures negative. Respiratory viral panel negative. ANCA and anti-GBM antibody negative. Treated with IV methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for three days, then oral prednisone 40 mg daily. Breathing improved and she weaned to room air before discharge.

Medication changes: methotrexate and folic acid STOPPED - do not restart without rheumatology. Ibuprofen STOPPED. Prednisone 40 mg daily, decrease by 10 mg every two weeks to 10 mg, then return to her usual 5 mg daily (hold the 5 mg tablets during the taper). Imatinib 400 mg daily continued. Lisinopril, calcium, vitamin D unchanged.

Follow-up: PCP within 1-2 weeks; pulmonology clinic with repeat CT in about 6-8 weeks; rheumatology regarding RA treatment.

Allergies: sulfa, latex.

documents.title: Outside Records Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary reviewed. Med list updated. TCM visit on 4/28.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call, discharged yesterday. Pt says breathing is easier than last week, still coughs some, no fever since Saturday, no blood coughed up. Has her prednisone 20 mg tablets and the taper calendar from the hospital. Understands no methotrexate and no ibuprofen. Visit booked 4/28. Discharge paperwork not yet received - requested.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit after 4/15-4/21 admission for diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.
Briefly: two weeks of dyspnea, dry cough and low fevers; ED sat 92%, crackles, CRP 25, ESR 40, LDH 220, CXR with bilateral interstitial infiltrates, HRCT with diffuse ground-glass, no PE. Bronch showed progressively bloody BAL with hemosiderin-laden macrophages; infectious studies, ANCA and anti-GBM negative. IV methylpred x3 then prednisone 40. Cause not pinned down.
Now: day 10 at 40 mg. Breathing better each day, walks the driveway without stopping. Cough fading. No hemoptysis.
Meds reconciled with the discharge summary: STOPPED methotrexate, folic acid, ibuprofen. Prednisone taper 40 > 30 > 20 > 10 every two weeks, then back to 5 mg (5 mg tabs on hold). Imatinib 400, lisinopril 10, calcium, D3 continue.
Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Exam: no distress. SpO2 96% RA. Heart regular. Lungs: a few faint crackles at both bases, much less than described in hospital. No edema. Joints quiet so far.
A/P:
1. DAH, improving. Taper as written. Pulm clinic with repeat CT in June - appointment confirmed. Return or ED for any hemoptysis or worse breathing.
2. RA off methotrexate - she has a rheum visit in May.
3. CML - imatinib continues; heme aware.
4. HTN - fine.
Labs today. See her in July.

documents.title: Lab Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Counts stable. Glucose ok on the taper. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Pharmacy Question
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacist called: pt has active scripts for both prednisone 20 mg and 5 mg and asked which is current. Explained the hospital taper, now at 20 mg daily, then 10 mg, then back to her 5 mg tablets in mid-June. Pharmacist satisfied.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up.
Finished the taper mid-June, back on prednisone 5 mg daily. No breathlessness, back on her usual walks including the hill. No cough. No hemoptysis.
Pulmonology 6/9: she reports the repeat CT was clear - the ground-glass is gone. Their letter not here yet.
Rheumatology in May: methotrexate stays off; joints quiet on prednisone alone for now, and they will talk about another medicine at her next visit. Nothing new started.
Heme: no change, imatinib continues.
Meds: imatinib 400, prednisone 5, calcium 600 BID, D3 2000, lisinopril 10. Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Exam: well. SpO2 97% RA. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema. Hands and wrists without synovitis; R popliteal fullness unchanged.
A/P: DAH - symptom-free, awaiting pulm letter. RA - rheum managing, no DMARD at present. CML stable. HTN controlled. Labs today. Follow-up in the fall.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Diane, Friday's labs look good: blood count is normal and kidney and liver tests are fine. Enjoy the rest of the summer and we'll see you in October.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Feeling like myself again.

reports.text: Non-contrast CT of the chest. Interval resolution of the previously seen diffuse ground-glass opacities. Lungs otherwise clear. No lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion.

documents.title: Pulmonology Clinic Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonology clinic - visit 06/09/2026

Seen in follow-up of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage diagnosed during her April admission. She has completed most of her prednisone taper and reports no dyspnea, cough or hemoptysis. Room-air saturation normal; lungs clear.

Repeat CT today: the diffuse ground-glass opacities have resolved.

No further pulmonary follow-up planned unless symptoms recur. Methotrexate remains off per rheumatology.

Allergies: sulfa, latex.

Pulmonology
